transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Lee. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate you taking the time. 

Um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right. I don't want to sound silly, and it's probably just my mind playing tricks on me, but I've been having this little issue lately. I've been hearing these... well, voices. They're actually quite clear. I mostly hear them when I'm in my apartment, and sometimes when I'm out, like if I wander into an empty room at a museum. 

It sounds just like women whispering from behind the walls, and they... they tell me which photographs belong in the archive. I know that probably sounds terribly strange, doesn't it? I try not to make a fuss about it, but I just wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by coming in to ask about it. Is that... is that the sort of thing I should be telling you?
How long have you been hearing these whispering voices—did they start days, weeks, or months ago?

Oh, um... well, I suppose it's been a little while. I hope I haven't waited too long to come in and bother you with it. I'd say it's been... maybe about eight months? Yes, roughly eight months now. 

And, um, along with the whispering, I've also had this... well, this certainty that people are watching my archive. I know that sounds a bit dramatic, doesn't it? I really have tried my best to just brush it off and keep it to myself so I wouldn't worry anyone. I hope I'm not wasting your time with all this... am I doing the right thing by telling you this now?

During these past eight months, have you also noticed periods where your mood was significantly low (like depression) or unusually high/energetic, alongside the voices and beliefs about being watched?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose I have. I hope it's okay to admit that. There was a time, not too long ago, where I just... I had so much energy. I felt wonderful, really, but maybe a bit too wonderful? I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours a night, but I wasn't tired at all. I was just rushing around, trying to organize everything for the archive, moving from one task to the next without stopping. 

And, um, yes, during that whole time, I was still hearing the women whispering behind the walls. And I was absolutely certain—I still am, really—that the museum board was tracking everything I was doing with the photographs. 

I know that probably sounds like I'm making a big deal out of nothing, or that I'm just terribly disorganized. I really hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you. Is that... is that the kind of mood change you were asking about?
Aside from that high-energy period, have you also heard the whispering voices or felt certain you were being watched during times when your mood was just normal—not unusually high or low?

Oh, yes... um, I have. I hope it's alright to say that. There was a stretch—maybe a few weeks or so—where I felt quite normal. I wasn't rushing about or feeling overly grand or anything like that. My mood was just... fine, really. 

But even then, when everything else was perfectly calm, I was still hearing the whispering in the apartment. And I... well, I was still absolutely certain that the arts people were monitoring my phone. I know it must sound so silly to hold onto a thought like that when I was otherwise feeling so level-headed. I tried my best to just ignore it and go about my day so I wouldn't be a bother to anyone. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Out of these full eight months, roughly how many weeks in total would you say you were in that high-energy, low-sleep state, compared to the time your mood was normal?

Oh, um... well, if I really think about it... I suppose it's been a fair bit of the time. I hope I'm not making myself sound completely out of control, but... well, those periods where I was barely sleeping, making all those racing plans, and just having that furious, rushing energy... I'd say that's taken up about six of the eight months. 

I know that sounds like an awful lot of time to be in such a state, doesn't it? I really did try to keep it contained, just focusing on my projects and spending a bit too much on supplies for the archive... I didn't want to cause a fuss or worry anyone. I hope I don't sound too dreadful admitting that it went on for that long. Is that... is that the sort of timeline you were looking for?

latest_inference.note: Manic episode with racing thoughts, decreased sleep, and grandiosity co-occurred with psychotic symptoms for 6 of 8 months (majority of illness duration), while psychotic symptoms (voices, delusions of surveillance) persisted for ~2 months without mood symptoms, meeting criteria for schizoaffective disorder and effectively ruling out schizophrenia alone (F20.9), since mood episodes are too prominent/persistent relative to psychosis-only periods for a primary psychotic disorder diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent auditory hallucinations (whispering voices) and persecutory delusions (being watched/monitored) for 8 months. During this period, she also experienced a manic episode (elevated mood, decreased need for sleep, increased energy, excessive activity, excessive spending) lasting about 6 of the 8 months, during which the psychotic symptoms continued. Critically, she also had a distinct period of at least 2 weeks where psychotic symptoms (hallucinations, delusions) persisted in the absence of any mood episode (normal mood, no mania). This pattern—concurrent mood episode and psychotic symptoms for a substantial portion of the illness, plus psychotic symptoms occurring for ≥2 weeks without a mood episode—meets criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder rather than a primary mood disorder with psychotic features (which would require psychosis only during mood episodes) or Schizophrenia (which would require mood symptoms to be a minor/brief part of the overall illness rather than present for the majority of the time). The manic-type mood episode with mixed features is not otherwise specified in detail, warranting the 'unspecified' code F25.9.
